title: Judge the Jewels: Taylor Swift Wears Both Antique and Antique-Inspired Jewelry Together at Toy Story 5 Premiere
text: Celebrity Jewelry Judge the Jewels: Taylor Swift Wears Both Antique and Antique-Inspired Jewelry Together at Toy Story 5 Premiere These thoughtful designs feel like the anthesis of the generic AI-fueled nothingness the internet bombards us with every day. Published 2 days ago on June 19, 2026 By INSTORE Staff Share Tweet View this post on Instagram A post shared by D’Orazio World (@dorazioworld) The sighting: Superstar songstress Taylor Swift recently attended the “Toy Story 5” premiere in a lovely Erdem dress. The singer paired the romantic look with a beautifully curated selection of vintage-inspired jewelry representing aesthetics from different eras as well one genuine antique piece. See More Jewelry Coverage of Taylor Swift The jewels: Here’s what we know Taylor Swift wore: Selim Mouzannar’s Gemma ring (listed online for $5,000 – $10,000). This sleek modern ring features an enamel halo, a detail reminiscent of Victorian era enameling. Miraki’s oval tennis bracelet in yellow gold (listed online starting at $3,380). This bracelet’s oval diamonds perfectly fit the vintage-inspired elongated gem trend. Le Vian Couture earrings in platinum and 18K yellow gold with diamonds and fancy light yellow diamonds (listed online for $11,797.50). These earrings are contemporary, but with a strong Art Deco feel. Her elongated old mine cut engagement ring with its engraved gold setting by Kindred Lubeck of Artifex Fine Jewelry. Jewelry credits from @TayorSwiftStyled, Le Vian, Miraki, and Sophie Jane Jewels. The trends: Antique and antique-inspired jewelry are the height of trendiness for 2026, partly due to Ms. Swift herself. And it’s not hard to understand why: these beautifully detailed, thoughtful designs feel like the anthesis of the generic, meaningless AI-fueled nothingness that the internet bombards us with more and more of every day. The Le Vian earrings also hit on the colored diamonds trend (aka Desert Diamonds). What do we think? I’m a little biased here because is this look completely in keeping with my own personal jewelry style. Mixing modern and vintage pieces as well as metals and designers? Yes, please. I even have my own antique diamond piece from Sophie Jane Jewels. Mine is an Art Deco ring, not a horseshoe pendant, but I’d wear that horseshoe in a heartbeat. This is just fantastic. It’s thoughtful and interesting but still feels personal. Can you tell I love it? I love it. Judgement: 1,000/10 for a look I’d cheerfully transfer directly to my own jewelry box.
